leads.title: Self-similar finite-time blowups with singular profiles of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model: theoretical and numerical investigations
leads.authors: De Huang, Jiajun Tong, Xiuyuan Wang
leads.claimed_content: Self-similar blowups of gCLM under a derivative-degeneracy condition on the data. For a > 0, ONE-scale self-similar blowups with regular profiles not previously found. For a <= 0, a two-scale scenario whose OUTER profile converges to a singular function while the inner profile stays regular on a smaller scale. The inner profile is governed by A TRAVELING WAVE on the smaller scale, and THE EXISTENCE OF THOSE TRAVELING WAVE SOLUTIONS IS ESTABLISHED RIGOROUSLY VIA A FIXED-POINT METHOD. 55 pages, 19 figures.
leads.why_it_matters: This is THE object Route-D has been building a certificate for. If the reading is right, existence of the two-scale inner traveling wave is already a theorem, and by an analytic fixed-point argument rather than a computer-assisted one. It would also place the two-scale scenario at a <= 0, while this project has been working it at a > 0.
must_verify: Is their inner traveling wave the same equation as this project's R = Omega H(Omega) - c Omega_X - a U Omega_X?
Does their fixed-point map use the first integral Omega = -(E/c)^{1/a}, or an inequivalent reduction?
Is their two-scale scenario really a <= 0 only? If so, what is this project's a > 0 two-scale object?
Do they state compact support and the order-1/a zero?
leads.confidence: identifiers high; technical content medium; the a-sign statement is the single most decision-relevant item and is LEAST verified

leads.title: Self-similar finite-time blowups with smooth profiles of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda model
leads.authors: De Huang, Jiajun Tong, Xiuyuan Wang
leads.claimed_content: gCLM admits exact self-similar finite-time blowups with interiorly smooth profiles for all a <= 1. The profiles are either smooth on the whole real line OR COMPACTLY SUPPORTED and smooth in the interior of their closed supports. Existence via the fixed point of an a-dependent nonlinear map R_a: if f is a fixed point then Omega(x) = -x f(x) is an exact self-similar profile, with c_l and c_omega given explicitly as integrals of f. Regularity, monotonicity and far-field decay characterized. The a = 0 and a = 1/2 profiles are strictly negative on (0, inf); the a = 1 profile is COMPACTLY SUPPORTED.
leads.why_it_matters: Compactly supported profiles in this family are established literature, not a discovery. Reducing the profile equation to a scalar fixed point with an explicit algebraic relation is the established technique here. v12's 'the profile ends' and v14's reduction are both inside known territory.
must_verify: Their R_a and its relation to the first integral
Whether compact support in their (self-similar) problem appears only at a = 1, and why that pattern differs from this project's two-scale problem where it appears at every a > 0
leads.confidence: identifiers high; technical content medium-high (the R_a description was quoted with unusual specificity)

leads.title: Steady-states and traveling-wave solutions of the generalized Constantin-Lax-Majda equation
leads.authors: Hisashi Okamoto, Takashi Sakajo, Marcus Wunsch
leads.claimed_content: Computes steady states and traveling waves of gCLM and describes their asymptotic behaviour; numerical evidence for non-trivial steady and traveling-wave solutions for every a > 0; relation to blow-up and to Benjamin-Ono discussed.
leads.why_it_matters: gCLM traveling waves have been computed since 2014. Any claim about their existence, shape or asymptotics needs to be positioned against this paper first.
must_verify: Whether the asymptotics they describe include the finite support radius X_c and the order-1/a zero
leads.confidence: identifiers high; technical content LOW (abstract-level only)

leads.title: On self-similar finite-time blowups of the De Gregorio model on the real line
leads.claimed_content: Infinitely many compactly supported self-similar solutions, distinct under rescaling, blowing up in finite time; omega in H^1(R), odd, supported on [-1, 1].
leads.why_it_matters: Further confirmation that compactly supported profiles in this family are standard. Note theirs are ODD and self-similar; this project's are EVEN traveling waves.
must_verify: parity and scaling class, to be sure it is a different object

leads.ref: multiple; incl. Chen-Hou 'Stable Nearly Self-Similar Blowup of the 2D Boussinesq and 3D Euler Equations with Smooth Data II: Rigorous Numerics', and CLM-family computer-assisted work
leads.claimed_content: Computer-assisted proofs using interval arithmetic (INTLAB) and Newton-Kantorovich are ESTABLISHED PRACTICE in exactly this family; asymptotically self-similar finite-time blowups of the one-scale form have been established for the CLM model by computer-assisted proof. Newton-Kantorovich plus a global bifurcation framework is used to prove exact solution branches.
leads.why_it_matters: THE SINGLE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT ITEM. This project's L1 -- 'a certified Level-2 computer-assisted blow-up profile for the 1D gCLM/HL toy model' -- is the thing these groups already do routinely. Finishing L1 would be a CAPABILITY demonstration and a reproduction, not a novel result. That is what standing brick (4) always said it was; the literature makes it explicit.
must_verify: exactly which a values and which scaling class have been certified for gCLM specifically
whether any published computer-assisted proof covers the TWO-SCALE traveling wave
leads.confidence: the general practice claim is high; the specific 'one-scale CLM already certified' claim is medium and matters most

leads.title: Stable Finite-Time Singularity Formation for 3D Navier-Stokes via 5D-Lifted Axisymmetric Reductions
leads.claimed_content: Claims finite-time singularity formation for 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes on the periodic torus: a stationary rescaled profile solving a nonlinear elliptic fixed-point equation in an analytically weighted Hilbert space, with computer-assisted Newton-Kantorovich validation by interval arithmetic, reconstructed into a nearly self-similar singular evolution and transferred to the torus.
leads.status: DO NOT USE, DO NOT REPEAT AS A RESULT. A solo preprint claiming a Clay Millennium Problem. Recorded ONLY so that a later session does not rediscover it and get excited. Extraordinary claims of this kind are overwhelmingly likely to contain an error, and nothing in this project should be re-planned around it unless and until it is accepted by the community.
must_verify: community reaction, published status, expert commentary -- NOT the mathematics, which is far outside what can be checked here
leads.confidence: the preprint exists and says this; its correctness is entirely unassessed and presumed doubtful

consequences_for_this_project: L1 as defined is very likely occupied territory. Finishing it is a capability demonstration, not a novel result.
v14's first integral must be presumed known until HTW23/HTW26 are read; the leg's mathematics is unaffected, its novelty framing is.

The a-sign question (is the two-scale scenario a <= 0 territory?) is the highest-value single thing to verify, because it bears on whether this project's a > 0 two-scale object is the right object at all.
Nothing here changes the two structural walls or the ~0.05% Clay odds.
